content:
jess: heads-up — saw a customer app hit degraded latency this morning when model-xl hit capacity. wanna decide if we should wire an automatic model-variant fallback (primary -> quantized) at the routing layer :thinking_face:

mike: definitely the right idea. question is: config surface — per-customer policy vs global tier defaults?

sara: from runtime pov fallback needs two things: (1) a compatibility map (model-xl -> model-xl-qt) and (2) KV cache transfer or cold-warm handling. otherwise we lose warmup benefits.

leo: ops concern: if we auto-fallback on saturation we might overload the fallback pool. need backpressure & circuit-breaker. also quota accounting should be clear to customers.

anya: product: customers expect predictable quality. auto fallback must be visible in console and in telemetry (we should annotate requests with fallback_reason). fallback should be opt-out for enterprise accounts.

mike: proposal: routing policy has fields: "enabled", "priority_conditions" (latency, capacity_pct), "fallback_sequence" (list of variant ids), "actuation_mode" (automatic/manual), "visibility" (telemetry+console). something like:

```
{
  "enabled": true,
  "priority_conditions": { "capacity_pct": 0.9, "p95_latency_ms": 500 },
  "fallback_sequence": ["model-xl-qt-v1", "model-xl-ptq-v2"],
  "actuation_mode": "auto",
  "visibility": "annotate_and_console"
}
```

jess: +1. also want a safe-window: only trigger if condition holds for N seconds and limit RPS of fallbacks to X/s to avoid surge.

sara: agree. runtime can do a two-step check: capacity signal from scheduler + model-level token throughput. if we see sustained saturation (10s) then switch to fallback route for new requests. ongoing requests stay on original model until completion.

leo: telemetry: we need metrics: fallback_count, fallback_rate_per_min, fallback_latency_delta, fallback_success_rate. also emit spans "route.decision" with fields reason=capacity, target=variant.

anya: console UX: show per-tenant routing policy with recent rollouts and a "what happened" timeline when fallbacks occur. default policy for free/tier customers could be more aggressive, enterprise conservative.

mike: API debate: should we expose this via our existing routing API or a new "fallbacks" top-level? I prefer extend existing route config to avoid new knobs. downside: more complex UI.

jess: extend existing route config is fine if we add a compact schema and validate. we also need a dry-run toggle so customers can preview fallback decisions (telemetry-only).

leo: ops: add a safety valve — if fallback pool CPU/GPU usage > 80% then stop auto-fallbacks and return 503 or queue. prefer circuit-breaker over silent routing to overloaded variants.

sara: implementation note: KV cache migration is hard. better to define fallback such that we only route to variants with compatible KV layout, and for others do cold-start with higher cost. log this in telemetry.

mike: will draft API shape and a minimal console wireframe. aiming for a canary rollout to internal tenants first.

jess: thanks. action items:
- mike: PR with schema + compatibility model to review (ETA 2d)
- sara: runtime changes doc for detection + actuation + cache handling (ETA 5d)
- leo: telemetry + circuit-breaker thresholds + SLO doc (ETA 3d)
- anya: console mockups + default policies per tier (ETA 4d)

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: please add link to canary runbook before enabling auto-mode on prod. :robot_face:

jess: cool — if anyone wants to jump in on the API shape ping me. will sync 11:30am PT if needed. :calendar:
